headline: Solid foundations with a few clear places to look next.

sections.title: What lined up well
sections.body: Inside the typical tour spread: how far the shoulders rotate at the top, how far the hips rotate at the top, how open the hips are at impact, how much the upper body leans at impact, how much the spine angle changes from setup to impact, how much the head drifts sideways.

sections.title: Worth a look
sections.body: Your the gap between shoulder turn and hip turn at the top measured less than most tour swings. Your how much the upper body leans at setup measured less than most tour swings. Your how bent the lead knee is at impact measured more than most tour swings. Your how much the hips slide toward the target measured less than most tour swings.

sections.title: Coach's read
sections.body:
Your shoulder turn at the top of the backswing, where the club changes direction, was in the tour range. Your hip turn at the top was also in the tour range. Your hip rotation at impact, the instant the club meets the ball, was in the tour range. Your posture, the spine and body angle held during the swing, stayed about as steady as a typical tour swing. Your tempo, the timing and rhythm of the swing, was close to the tour-typical pace.

At impact, your hips slid toward the target less than most tour swings. There is a lot of good motion here already.

sections.title: How to read this
sections.body: Every number here is measured from your video against a 400-swing tour reference — nothing is estimated by the AI. Ask the coach about any metric for the full story.
